newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria hikes par of deposit guarantee bond issue.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria hikes par of deposit guarantee bond issue.

text.p: Bulgaria's Finance Ministry raised the par of one of the two government bond issues placed in June to compensate depositors in five banks slated for bankruptcy, the central bank (BNB) said.

"The finance ministry increased by 2,461.864 million levs to 6,301.174 million levs the par value of the seven-year T-bond issue numbered BG 2040496221, which was placed with the State Savings Bank," a BNB statement said.
The issue with an initial par of 3,839.310 million levs, was placed on June 27 and matures on June 19, 2003.
The issue bears a semi-annual coupon equal to the BNB's central interest rate (CIR) for the period to maturity.
The CIR was set at 25 percent monthly or 300 percent annually from September 24, up from previous 108 percent.
The par is to be paid in seven equal annual instalments and interest due is to be calculated each time on the remainder of the principal.
Under Bulgaria's deposit guarantee law the State Savings Bank repays lev deposits of companies and individuals in local banks against which the central bank has filed insolvency suits.
The SSB can also use these bonds as a collateral against borrowing from the BNB. -- Anastas Petrov, Sofia Newsroom, 359-2-84561 REU
